sector: Specialty coffee roaster and cafe selling stickers and merchandise at the till, at farmers markets and to wholesale accounts.
founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon, a converted machine shop with one counter, two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts.
about: Meridian and Ash roast single origin coffee in a converted machine shop and sell it across their own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. The merchandise table is half the fun: stickers people put on laptops and water bottles because they actually like the mark. The whole point is a range that feels made by hand, not bought by the case.
audience: Cafe regulars twenty to thirty five who buy a sticker at the till without deciding first, and wholesale buyers who hand them out with orders.
price_positioning: Impulse retail, three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack. Priced to be handed out by the fistful, so the range has to read as abundant rather than precious.
typography: A shaded serif wordmark that looks painted rather than set, arched over a filled roundel. Text and labels lean into a friendly, slightly irregular hand. Nothing boutique or foil thin.
voice: Plain, warm, a little wry, never precious. Example line: Pull one off the sheet, stick it on your laptop, come back for the other three.
brand_assets_status: No usable source files exist. The window mark was hand painted on the shop glass in 2018 by a sign painter who never handed over a file. The three current illustrations survive only printed on the coffee bags, and the printer still holds last season's counter card artwork.
values: Consistency people can trust, so the artwork stops being redrawn slightly differently every batch, and a hand made feel that reads as a real roastery rather than a franchise.
